conviction_note: The stock is down 40% in 20 sessions on the DayOne IPO pause, the Nov 16 BIS remote-access rule and Alibaba's warning about its capex. Those are known and largely priced. What the print adds is Q3 bookings against the 1 GW target, which counterparty capex (Tencent, Alibaba) supports, plus management's first word on DayOne. So the findings sum to +1.5 and the scaled number is +1.2 (p_up 55 x abs 12). The moderate put skew (+5.25) and Alibaba's capex warning keep p_up near 50.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about US$464-474M / RMB ~3.19-3.22B. Sources: Benzinga $464.1M (https://es.benzinga.com/quote/GDS/earnings-forecasts), MarketBeat-style $468.74M (https://www.dailypolitical.com/?p=10578734), Stocktwits $467.21M, Earnings Whispers $474.4M (https://finviz.com/news/424958/gds-must-prove-its-1-gigawatt-bookings-surge-is-real-after-stock-halves), Chartmill RMB3.191B (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/GDS/estimates). This sits at the run-rate implied by the company's FY2026 guide of RMB12.7-13.0B (H2 implied RMB6.245-6.545B; https://finviz.com/news/381706/gds-holdings-limited-reports-second-quarter-2026-results). The EPS bar is disputed, ranging from -$0.24 to +$1.34 per ADS across sources, so nothing here is sized on EPS. The line the stock trades on is bookings (FY target 1 GW, H1 471 MW), for which there is no published consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest was 14.54M ADS-equivalents as of 2026-10-30, 6.2 days to cover, about 7.2% of 200.93M shares outstanding (https://massive.com/quote/gds.md). That is up from 11.45M on 2026-09-30 (https://massive.com/quote/GDS). Elevated and building, but not a crowded 18-23% short. Skew_25d is +5.25 vol points (moderate downside paid), the event-implied move is 9.44%, 20d realised vol is 104%, and put/call OI is 0.70. Spot $13.615 is 2% above the 52-week low and -71% from the high. The stock ran +12.5% on 2026-11-23 with no company news and gave about 10% back on 11-24.

findings.finding: Q3 bookings are likely to keep pace with the 1 GW FY2026 target. H1 2026 bookings were a record 471 MW (260 MW in Q2), with 600 MW of further reservations and year-end reservations guided above 1 GW, so about 530 MW is needed in H2. The direct customers' Q3 spend supports conversion: Tencent's Q3 capex was RMB81.4B (+527% YoY, +54% QoQ) with cloud +35% 'as compute supply expanded', and Alibaba's Sep-quarter capex was RMB50.5B (+60%) with AI cloud revenue +53%. The market is openly doubting the target: the Earnings Whispers preview is headlined 'must prove its 1-gigawatt bookings surge is real after stock halves'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Q2 2026 (2026-08-13), record 260 MW bookings and a 1 GW target raise sent the ADS +6.2% to $34.77 (https://www.itiger.com/news/1121710048). On Q3 2025 a beat with weak bookings fell -5.05% (https://www.itiger.com/news/1183942273). Bookings is the line this name pays on.
findings.why_not_priced: The ADS is down 40% in 20 days and sits $13.6 against a $48 consensus target, a price that assumes the bookings run-rate breaks. If the market believed about 250 MW was booked in Q3, it would not trade 2% above its 52-week low with put skew bid. The Q3 bookings number itself is unpublished until the release.
findings.independence: Counterparty capex is a proxy, not GDS's own number. Tencent: https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3374902/tencent-profit-dips-sixfold-increase-ai-infrastructure-spending-sacrifices-margin (2026-11-18). Alibaba: https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/826516 (2026-11-19). VNET took a 60 MW order from a leading cloud provider in Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001508475/000110465926130769/tm2630453d1_ex99-1.htm).

findings.finding: Alibaba, one of GDS's three largest hyperscale customers, said on its 2026-11-19 call that the new US compute export rules 'may lead to a downward revision of that long-term 20 gigawatt target', with an associated reduction in overall capex. It gave no new figure. The call will ask GDS whether its 2027+ bookings and reservations hold, and any softening of the 1 GW or reservations language lands on the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior GDS print in which a top customer cut capex has been located. GDS fell into a new 52-week low on Nov 18-20, the week of the Alibaba call (https://longbridge.com/en/news/306357025).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell through Nov 19-20. What is not priced is whether GDS's reservations from Alibaba are affected. The 20 GW target is global and includes overseas capacity, which is what the rule restricts, so the domestic read-through is unresolved until GDS speaks.
findings.independence: Tencent's president said the restrictions could slow its next model near term and encourage domestic supply chains (https://letsdatascience.com/news/tencent-third-quarter-profit-falls-6-as-ai-capex-jumps-sixfo-779719ee). That is mixed for domestic data center demand.

findings.finding: DayOne, GDS's large non-controlling equity investee (35.6% per Q2 call summaries), paused its planned US IPO of up to $5B (Bloomberg, 2026-11-20). ByteDance is about 69% of DayOne's revenue. The 2026-11-16 BIS interim rule requires licences for advanced chips going to Malaysia/Singapore data centers and to any data center supplying significant compute to China-headquartered firms; existing such centers must obtain a licence within 90 days. The GDS call will be management's first word on DayOne's exposure and on the stake's value.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is not an earnings line. On non-earnings days GDS fell 16% on Mon 2026-11-16 (rule) and 8% on Fri 2026-11-20 (IPO pause) (https://longbridge.com/en/news/306357025).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the two days above cost about 23%. What remains unpriced is management's quantification (licence status for ByteDance halls in Johor, IPO timing, any equity-method write-down). It could go either way, hence the wide two-sided band.
findings.independence: BIS rule detail: https://www.gtlaw.com/de/insights/2026/11/bis-interim-final-rule-targets-remote-access-to-advanced-semiconductors-rescinds-ai-diffusion-rule (2026-11). ByteDance 69% of DayOne sales: https://aiweekly.co/alerts/dayone-pauses-5b-us-ipo-as-bytedance-drives-69-of-sales

findings.finding: The FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guide looks conservative against the run-rate. H1 adjusted EBITDA was RMB3,354.7M (Q1 1,948.7 including one-time items; Q2 1,406.0). The raised FY guide of RMB5,900-6,100M implies H2 of RMB2,545-2,745M, or about 1,273-1,373 per quarter, below Q2's 1,406. Revenue consensus of about RMB3.19B sits at the guide-midpoint run-rate. A Q3 at or near Q2's EBITDA level leaves room to hold or raise the range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 raised revenue and EBITDA guides alongside bookings and the stock rose 6.2%. Q3 2025 reaffirmed the guide and the stock fell 5%. Q3 is seasonally soft on margin: Q3 2025 adjusted EBITDA was -2.2% QoQ (https://finviz.com/news/233563/gds-holdings-limited-reports-third-quarter-2025-results).
findings.why_not_priced: This is arithmetic on public guidance that sits inside what the company guided, so it is mostly expected. It is sized small for that reason. If the market expected a raise, consensus FY revenue would not sit below the guide ($1.84B vs $1.88-1.93B per Earnings Whispers).
findings.independence: Consensus FY revenue below guide: https://finviz.com/news/424958/gds-must-prove-its-1-gigawatt-bookings-surge-is-real-after-stock-halves. Shares the Q2 release with finding 1.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is washed out and short interest is building. Short interest rose from 11.45M (2026-09-30) to 14.54M (2026-10-30), 6.2 days to cover, and the ADS fell 32.7% in the week to Nov 20 on sector and regulatory news with no company announcement. It then rose 12.5% intraday on 2026-11-23 on no GDS news, showing how violently it reprices on any reassurance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No earnings-day positioning history is available (baseline history untrustworthy). The non-earnings moves of -16%, -8% and +12.5% in the last 7 sessions show the scale.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew (+5.25) and the 52-week low say the market is positioned for more downside. A short base built during October would have to cover into any guide-hold, which is not in a price that sits 2% above the low.
findings.independence: Weekly recap (32.71% weekly fall, no company announcements): https://longbridge.com/en/news/306357025

findings.finding: The first post-IPO C-REIT asset injection had not closed by 2026-11-04: the Southern GDS data center REIT (508060) still held one asset, the Kunshan Guojin data center, per its SSE notice. Q3 therefore probably carries no deconsolidation gain like Q3 2025's RMB1,369M. A GAAP EPS consensus of $1.31/ADS (Earnings Whispers) that assumes gains may produce a headline 'miss'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Q2 2026 Earnings Whispers called a 61% EPS miss and the stock still rose 6.2%. GAAP EPS headlines have not driven this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The EPS bar is disputed (-$0.24 to +$1.34), so any headline miss is noise. Capped small.
findings.independence: The Q2 release says the injection was 'under regulatory review' (https://finviz.com/news/381706/gds-holdings-limited-reports-second-quarter-2026-results).

findings.finding: Peer VNET's Q3 2026 (released 2026-11-23, before GDS) showed wholesale revenue +27.6% YoY, a 60 MW order from a leading cloud provider and its FY2026 guide maintained. Wholesale utilisation slipped to 70.7% from 73.9% (ramp sites 25.5%), consistent with demand intact but move-ins slow.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GDS rose about 12.5% on 2026-11-23, the day of VNET's print (https://massive.com/quote/gds.md).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced on Nov 23 and then partly given back on Nov 24. It is a peer, not a counterparty.

findings.finding: GDS plans to invest more than RMB30B in Ulanqab over five years (reported 2026-11-17, HK shares -8.5% intraday). Q2 had already raised FY2026 capex to about RMB10B from 9B, against roughly 4.7x net debt/EBITDA. A 2027 capex signal on the call adds to leverage worries, although it funds bookings that are pre-committed (89.2% pre-commitment rate on area under construction).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HK -8.5% intraday on 2026-11-17 (https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1703758.shtml). No earnings-day history on capex surprises was found.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced on 11-17. It is filed as a question per the financing rule: the spend funds pre-committed capacity (89.2% pre-commitment under construction), so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Q2 release capex raise and pre-commitment rate: https://finviz.com/news/381706/gds-holdings-limited-reports-second-quarter-2026-results

findings.finding: The Nov 16 BIS rule restricts Chinese firms' access to compute in overseas data centers, which pushes China hyperscalers' AI capacity back to the mainland, where GDS operates. Management can frame this as incremental domestic demand on the call. This is an inference not yet confirmed by GDS or a customer, beyond Tencent's remark that it encourages domestic supply chains over time.
findings.why_not_priced: The market traded the rule as a negative for GDS through DayOne (-16% on 11-16) without crediting a domestic offset. Domestic chip supply, not data center space, is the binding constraint, so this is sized small.

findings.finding: Reuters (via etnet, 2026-11-18) reported the US will advance plans to ban imports of Chinese data center equipment. GDS fell 5% in HK that day and the market tied the move to its supply chain. GDS's capacity is overwhelmingly in mainland China, so a US import ban does not touch its operations directly.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced on 11-18. It is off-line for GDS's China business. Filed because the call may address it.

outside_window.finding: Existing data centers already supplying China-headquartered firms must obtain a BIS licence within 90 days of the Nov 2026 rule's effective date. The outcome for DayOne's ByteDance halls in Johor resolves around Feb 2027.
DayOne may still pursue its IPO in 2027 if sentiment improves. A relisting attempt or a smaller deal would revalue GDS's stake.

baseline_tension: The skew (+5.25, downside paid) and a -40% 20-day run-up both point down, and my small positive lean cuts against the skew. The reasons are that the negatives the skew prices (DayOne IPO pause, BIS rule, Alibaba capex caveat) are already public and cost the stock about 40%, while the print's own line, bookings, is the one this name paid on last time. p_up is held at 55, not higher, because Alibaba's warning is a direct-customer negative on the same line.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (proxy smaller): the bookings finding rests on counterparty capex, not a GDS number, so +2.5 became +2.0.

Rule 6 (inside guidance): the EBITDA-guide arithmetic sits inside the company's guided range, so +1.0 became +0.7. The EPS-based C-REIT finding was kept capped at -0.3 because the EPS bar is disputed.
Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission): the domestic-shift inference went from +0.5 to +0.3.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the Ulanqab capex finding went from -0.5 to -0.4 after checking that it funds pre-committed capacity.

Lessons recap: the base rate was rebuilt from confirmed releases (Q2 2026 +6.2%, Q3 2025 -5.05%) because the baseline history was untrustworthy. I also added the US import-ban item at -0.2, filed rather than left out.
p_up and abs_move were unchanged: 55 and 12.
